task: Build the Phase 25.2 compiler with Clang 18 and mold using the repository Makefile.
observation: Clang selected an incomplete GCC 14 installation with no C++ standard headers although GCC 13 headers were installed. The initial compile failed at <algorithm>; explicitly selecting the valid GCC 13 installation allowed Clang compilation and mold linking. The Makefile now selects the newest installed GCC directory with matching C++ headers when invoking Clang.
impact: The configured Clang executable was present but the default driver could not compile this project on the host until its C++ standard-library path was corrected.
evidence: make -B CXX=clang++ ... first failed: src/moss.cpp:1:10: fatal error: 'algorithm' file not found
clang++ --gcc-install-dir=/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/13 -std=c++17 -fuse-ld=mold ... completed a real compiler build

resolution.summary: Makefile discovers an installed GCC toolchain directory whose matching C++ headers exist, while keeping CXX overrideable for GCC and other toolchains.

suggestion: Retain a portable Clang standard-library discovery path and verify actual linker selection in CI.

task: Verify configuration-safe object builds and the explicit GCC compatibility override during the Clang/mold multi-TU migration.
observation: The isolated Make regression confirmed separate Clang/GCC object directories but initially showed that switching back from GCC could leave the shared moss-dev output linked by GCC: its timestamp was newer than the preserved Clang objects, so Make skipped relinking. An active-link config stamp now records the compiler/flags associated with each public executable path and triggers a relink when configurations switch; the regression checks Clang-to-GCC-to-Clang and confirms ordinary no-op builds remain unchanged.
impact: Without the active-link stamp, configuration-specific objects alone did not prevent a stale executable from being reused after a toolchain switch.
evidence: Initial GCC override Make regression created a separate dev object directory but overwrote build/compiler/moss-dev.
Switch-back regression failed before the stamp because the Clang object timestamps were older than the GCC-linked output.
python3 tests/tooling/check_make_incremental_dependencies.py passes after the stamp, including Clang-to-GCC-to-Clang, PCH edits, and no-op checks.

resolution.summary: Make tracks the active build configuration next to the preserved executable path and relinks on configuration changes without adding the config file to the linker inputs.

tool_used: GNU Make and Python isolated build regression
suggestion: Keep toolchain-switch-back behavior in regression tests whenever multiple configurations share public executable paths.
